Early on, the user called Customer.io an email marketing system that 'felt designed for the data-savvy marketer'. With a good analytics plan you could build strong workflows. Building, editing and previewing emails felt straightforward and intuitive. Signup was easy with no sales call, and the whole system was running within two weeks.

Early pricing 'wasn't cheap, but felt fair'. The user didn't feel locked into a long-term contract and could scale cost with actual usage. They liked it enough to regularly demo their setup to co-workers.

Later complaints after what the user suspects was a Series A or leadership change: a price hike based on contact count rather than actual email usage, unsolicited Account Executive outreach, being pushed onto an annual commitment plan, removal of any way to sign in and test the product, and annual AE calls with 'fake promises to get the signature'. 'We're leaving.'
A developer got frustrated with Customer.io's limitations and built an open-source alternative instead. It defines segments in SQL, email flows in TypeScript, and templates in React+Tailwind.

'We used customer.io for the past few months but due to bugs with the system, we switched to sendwithus with sendgrid as our ESP. We've been really happy with the results.' (posted in a thread about an extended Customer.io outage)
